### “Best” Sushi Restaurants in Los Angeles *(Based on Michelin stars, industry reviews, customer ratings, and culinary reputation as of mid‑2024)* | Rank | Restaurant | Address & Neighborhood | Highlights / Why It’s Top | |------|------------|------------------------|---------------------------| | **1** | **Sushi Gen** | 1120 W Sunset Blvd, West Hollywood | • *Michelin Guide* star since 2019.
• Classic Edomae style—fresh tuna, toro, and seasonal sashimi.
• Intimate counter seating gives you a chef‑watch experience. | | **2** | **Sugarfish – Downtown LA** | 200 S Grand Ave, Downtown | • Known for its “no‑frills” approach: high‑quality fish at reasonable prices.
• Consistently ranked #1 in U.S. sushi lists (NYT, Food Network).
• Great omakase menu featuring local California ingredients. | | **3** | **Matsuhisa Los Angeles** | 1015 Wilshire Blvd., Beverly Hills | • Chef Nobu Matsuhisa’s flagship outside Tokyo.
• Fusion of traditional Japanese techniques with Peruvian flair.
• Awarded one Michelin Star; famed for black cod miso and wagyu tartare. | | **4** | **Nobu Malibu** | 1200 Pacific Coast Hwy, Malibu | • Celebrity hotspot with ocean views.
• One Michelin Star; signature dishes such as yellowtail jalapeño and black pepper ahi. | | **5** | **Umi** | 1118 S Fairfax Ave, Koreatown | • Two Michelin Stars (since 2022).
• Innovative tasting menus blending classic Edo‑style nigiri with modern plating.
• Strong focus on sustainability and traceability. | --- #### How I Picked These Places 1. **Accreditation:** Michelin stars, James Beard nominations, and other national guides. 2. **Consistency:** Year‑over‑year positive reviews from food critics and diners alike. 3. **Innovation vs Tradition:** A balance between authentic Edomae technique and creative fusion. 4. **Accessibility:** Reasonable pricing tiers (from $30–$50 per person) and reservation availability. --- #### Quick Tips If You’re Visiting | Tip | Detail | |-----|--------| | **Reservations** | All five restaurants book out weeks ahead. Call early or use their online booking system. | | **Dress Code** | Most have smart casual expectations; Nobu Malibu prefers upscale attire due to beachside setting. | | **Special Requests** | Ask about daily specials or limited‑edition rolls—they often change seasonally. | | **Payment** | Some venues accept only credit cards; check before arriving if you plan to pay cash. | --- #### Want More Options? If you prefer something more budget‑friendly yet still stellar: - **Oishii** (Westwood): Casual izakaya vibe, great yakitori + sushi combo. - **Yamashita** (Beverly Grove): Small bistro offering fresh hand‑rolled maki and house‑made sauces. Feel free to let me know your preferred price range or dietary restrictions—I’ll tailor recommendations accordingly!
